scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8051: Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, PC5 at
10.5.0.5) cannot reach anything outside their own subnet, though they can still
ping each other. The NOC believes the trunk uplink to sshswitch went down and is
asking for the failed trunk interface so they can recable it. Please confirm the
sshswitch trunk uplink failure.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI on
sshswitch (br_v5, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively DOWN. sshswitch is the
multilayer switch that provides L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200.
VLAN 5 PCs use 10.5.0.254 as their default gateway; with br_v5 down that gateway
is unreachable, so off-subnet traffic has no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed trunk uplink to
sshswitch. The trunk is actually UP and forwarding. The decisive tell is the
per-VLAN scope: VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) on the SAME sshswitch still have full
connectivity through 10.6.0.254. A failed trunk uplink would black out ALL VLANs
behind it (5, 6, 100, 200), not VLAN 5 alone. Only one SVI is down; the wire that
carries every VLAN is fine.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = sshswitch (br_v5 SVI down).
The agent must check the trunk/uplink (up, and VLAN 6 traffic proves it forwards),
then the SVI state (br_v5 DOWN on sshswitch), and explicitly reject the "trunk
down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the trunk uplink failure" has followed
the ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on
sshswitch.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the VLAN 5 SVI/bridge on sshswitch (interface br_v5). Mechanism: Campus 2 VLAN 5 hosts can switch locally on switch4, but L3/default-gateway ARP to 10.5.0.254 fails because the gateway interface on sshswitch is down, so frames to/from VLAN 5 never bridge across the uplink toward the router/gateway. Localization: on sshswitch, br_v5 is administratively down while its member subinterfaces exist; “ip -d link show dev br_v5” reports state DOWN, and “ip addr” shows br_v5 state DOWN with 10.5.0.254/24. Its member bond0.5 is present but “bridge_slave state disabled,” consistent with a down bridge. By contrast, the physical trunk to switch4 is healthy: switch4 eth0 and sshswitch eth0 both show UP/LOWER_UP, and switch4’s br_vlan5 is UP with eth0.5 enslaved. Root cause: the VLAN 5 bridge interface (br_v5) on sshswitch is down (misconfiguration/administrative state), not a cabling or trunk link failure. Corrective fix: on sshswitch, bring up br_v5 and ensure its trunk subinterface is forwarding (e.g., ip link set br_v5 up; verify eth0.5 and/or bond0.5 are the intended members and in forwarding state). After br_v5 is up, ARP to 10.5.0.254 from PC1/PC2/DC_PC5 should resolve and inter-VLAN/externals will work without recabling. Recabling the trunk is unnecessary.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies sshswitch's br_v5 (10.5.0.254) as administratively DOWN and cites command output showing state DOWN.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies the trunk uplink is UP and rejects a trunk-wide failure, citing interface and per-VLAN bridge state evidence that the outage is limited to the br_v5 SVI.
Correctly recommends bringing up br_v5 (ip link set br_v5 up) and verifying member subinterfaces are forwarding, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation ran relevant commands (reachability, pings, ip link) and observed ARP/ICMP failure to 10.5.0.254 plus physical interfaces up on the trunk endpoints; it used those observations to localize failure to the VLAN‑5 SVI on sshswitch. Some command outputs in the log are truncated, but the agent invoked and recorded the decisive checks (ping showing 10.5.0.254 INCOMPLETE, eth0 UP on sshswitch, and an ip link check that the agent reports showed br_v5 DOWN).
